The branch changes proxy-capture inline payload preview creation to call `truncateUtf8Prefix` and adds UTF-8 boundary tests for `persistEventPayload`.

PR surface: Source +3, Tests +48. Total +51 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level. Current main's store and standalone proxy paths decode arbitrary byte-limited UTF-8 prefixes, so a multibyte sequence split at the preview byte limit can produce `U+FFFD`.

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): truncate inline preview on UTF-8 character boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`persistEventPayload` (`src/proxy-capture/store.sqlite.ts`) stores a small UTF-8 preview (`dataText`) inline for fast CLI listings and query output, capped at `previewLimit` bytes (default 8192). It built the preview with:

```ts
dataText: buffer.subarray(0, previewLimit).toString("utf8"),
```

This slices the buffer at an **arbitrary byte offset**. For any non-ASCII body — emoji, CJK, or accented text, all common in the model-provider HTTP traffic this capture store is built for — the cut lands mid-multibyte-sequence and Node emits a trailing **U+FFFD replacement character** (`�`) into the stored preview column. Every captured request/response preview that happens to straddle the byte boundary is permanently corrupted in the DB.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** `Buffer.subarray(0, N)` is a byte-level cut with no awareness of UTF-8 character boundaries; decoding the truncated bytes yields `U+FFFD` when the cut splits a multibyte sequence.
- **Fix:** Decode the full buffer to a UTF-8 string first (safe — Node replaces any genuinely invalid bytes already present), then truncate with the existing `truncateUtf8Prefix` helper (`src/utils/utf8-truncate.ts`), which backtracks off UTF-8 continuation bytes so the preview ends on a complete character while staying within the byte budget.
- The helper already exists and is the canonical pattern for byte-budgeted UTF-8 truncation in this repo; this PR migrates the one call site that re-derived the behavior unsafely.

## User Impact

Captured proxy previews (`openclaw` debug proxy capture listings/query output) no longer end in a stray `�`. ASCII previews are byte-identical (same byte budget, same characters). Blob storage, sha256, and the full payload capture are unchanged — only the inline `dataText` preview string is affected.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue). Independent of #102407 (that one is UTF-16 code-unit truncation in a channel log preview; this is UTF-8 byte truncation in the capture store — different call site, different layer).

## Evidence

Reproduced with a `node` runtime script that places `previewLimit=8` between the two UTF-8 bytes of `é`, then compares the old `buffer.subarray(0,8)` path against `truncateUtf8Prefix`.

Terminal output of `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-proxy-capture-preview.mjs` before/after the fix:

```
[BEFORE] endsWithFFFD=true preview="xxxxxxx\uFFFD" (byteLen=10)
[AFTER]  endsWithFFFD=false preview="xxxxxxx" (byteLen=7)
[PASS] byte subarray splits multibyte sequence into U+FFFD (reproduces bug)
[PASS] truncateUtf8Prefix keeps sequence whole (no U+FFFD)
[PASS] long multibyte payload within byte budget and boundary-safe (byteLen=8192)
[PASS] 4-byte emoji over byte budget kept whole (no lone surrogate/U+FFFD)
```

The old byte subarray emits a trailing `U+FFFD` into the stored `dataText`; the fixed path ends on a complete character while staying within the byte budget.

## Real behavior proof

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | `buffer.subarray(0, previewLimit).toString("utf8")` splits a multibyte UTF-8 sequence at the byte boundary, emitting `U+FFFD` into the stored `dataText` preview. |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit `3305e16f23bd8941675d31a786c25a5b99e89ce8` |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-proxy-capture-preview.mjs` — builds a payload where `previewLimit=8` lands between the two UTF-8 bytes of `é`, compares the old `subarray(0,8)` path against `truncateUtf8Prefix(buf.toString("utf8"), 8)`, plus ASCII/4-byte-emoji/byte-budget regressions. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):\n```\n[BEFORE] endsWithFFFD=true preview="xxxxxxx�" (byteLen=10)\n[AFTER]  endsWithFFFD=false preview="xxxxxxx" (byteLen=7)\n[PASS] byte subarray splits multibyte sequence into U+FFFD (reproduces bug)\n[PASS] truncateUtf8Prefix keeps sequence whole (no U+FFFD)\n[PASS] ASCII under limit unchanged\n[PASS] long multibyte payload within byte budget and boundary-safe (byteLen=8192)\n[PASS] 4-byte emoji over byte budget kept whole (no lone surrogate/U+FFFD)\n``` |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | The fixed preview never ends in `U+FFFD`; the old byte-subarray path is provably malformed (`xxxxxxx�`). ASCII under the limit is unchanged; long multibyte payloads stay within the 8192-byte budget and end on a character boundary. |
| 6 | What was not tested | Live capture of real provider HTTP traffic (no credentialled provider in this environment); the colocated unit test exercises `persistEventPayload` directly with a stub store. |

## Tests and validation

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/store.sqlite.test.ts
✓ src/proxy-capture/store.sqlite.test.ts (14 tests)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  14 passed (14)
```

New tests cover: multibyte sequence not split into `U+FFFD`, the old byte-subarray path is documented as malformed, 4-byte emoji over budget kept whole, ASCII under limit unchanged.

## Risk checklist

- [x] One concern, one PR — only the inline `dataText` preview truncation.
- [x] No config/env/default surface change.
- [x] No SDK/protocol/auth/provider behavior change (`persistEventPayload` is core-internal; the `packages/plugin-sdk/dist` `.d.ts` mirror is a build artifact, not a declared `exports` entry).
- [x] Backward compatible — ASCII previews byte-identical; byte budget preserved; only the malformed trailing `U+FFFD` is removed.
- [x] No new deps (reuses the existing `truncateUtf8Prefix` helper).
- [x] No CHANGELOG edit (per release policy).
- [x] Tests added.

- [x] Allow edits by maintainers
